appraisal_events.evidence: Une dame dit sur la digue : « C'est une amie de la petite Simonet » avec l'air de précision avantageuse... et aussitôt on avait senti sur la figure de la personne à qui on apprenait cela une curiosité de mieux regarder la personne favorisée... Un privilège assurément qui ne paraissait pas donné à tout le monde.
appraisal_events.explanation: A stranger's remark on the promenade treats friendship with 'la petite Simonet' as a mark of local distinction, comparable to being linked to an aristocratic name, and visibly sharpens another listener's interest in whoever bears that connection.

status_effects.explanation: Being named as her friend is treated by an onlooker as a notable social privilege, marking 'la petite Simonet' as a locally prestigious figure among the young people at Balbec.

ambiguities: The narrator does not yet know which of the girls he had seen is 'la petite Simonet'; the reference sheet resolves the surname to Albertine, but this identification is not confirmed within the passage itself.
